correctness.rationale: Exact exchangeable pair counting yields ab(w-uv). The falling-factorial cross product is exactly -t, making every product factor <=1 and at least one <1 on the stated domain; remaining edge counts give exact zero. Bernoulli cross events share precisely one cell and yield strictly positive covariance. Uniform Taylor expansions of the explicit factors derive the sparse covariance and each side variance; direct rational exhaustive enumeration through 4x4 and 17,150 packaged checks reproduce the claims, not replacing the all-size proof.

value.rationale: Cross-part isolation is a natural statistic for bipartite random networks and matrix occupancy. Conditioning on precisely the edge total changes a shared-edge positive cross covariance into a strictly negative one at every nondegenerate finite k and suppresses sparse cross-part covariance from order n to order one; the balanced correlation asymptotics (positive nonzero limit versus negative constant/n) exhibit a measurable ensemble distinction. This structure is not a mere numerical table or an arbitrary degree class increment.
